Jack's Daily News

No. 21· 2 November 2026· Global, Italy in focus· Illustrated edition
In three lines

  1. Reddit and Pinterest post their strongest quarters in years on October 29, the same day WPP's revenue barely moves, the clearest evidence yet that platforms built around a specific community outearn ones selling generic reach.

  2. Google starts showing ads inside AI Mode's follow-up questions in the US, and Italy's own ad market data explains exactly why publishers are nervous about that: 88.6% of the country's "pure digital" ad spend already flows straight to platforms.

  3. Jennifer Lawrence doesn't endorse a haircare brand, she co-designs one with a biotech company that Chanel and Olaplex have already backed with 78 million dollars.

The world

Reddit investor letter / SEC 8-K · October 29, 2026

Reddit posts its strongest quarter yet and joins the S&P 500

Reddit's Q3 2026 revenue reached $895 million, up 53% year on year, with advertising revenue at $847 million, up 54%. Net income was $283 million, a 32% margin, and diluted EPS of $1.40 was up 75% year on year. Daily Active Uniques grew 12% to 130.3 million and Weekly Active Uniques grew 16% to 515.2 million. The company was added to the S&P 500 during the quarter.

Why it mattersReddit's whole business model is built on communities people already trust, not a feed optimized for maximum reach. That distinction is now showing up directly in the numbers, not just in the pitch deck.
Pinterest SEC 8-K / WPP Q3 Trading Update · October 29, 2026

Pinterest hits an all-time high of 661 million users the same day WPP's revenue barely moves

Pinterest's Q3 2026 revenue grew 12% to $1,174 million, with global monthly active users up 10% year on year to 661 million, an all-time high; CEO Bill Ready credited "differentiated AI-driven visual search and shopping experiences." On the same day, WPP's Q3 trading update showed group revenue of £3,274 million, up just 0.5%, with revenue less pass-through costs down 2.1% like-for-like and the Creative division down 4.9% in H1 2026. CEO Cindy Rose called it progress toward "a simpler, more unified WPP," still working through the holding company's turnaround plan.

Why it matterstwo platforms built around a specific audience (visual search intent, niche communities) posted record or near-record numbers the same day a generalist agency holding company reported revenue barely moving. It's the same split as Omnicom beating PepsiCo's old media account out of Coca-Cola while McDonald's walked away from FIFA (issue 20): owning something specific is outperforming selling reach at scale.
blog.google / Search Engine Land · October 28, 2026

Google starts putting ads inside AI Mode's follow-up questions

Google rolled out "multiturn ads" in AI Mode in the US: sponsored results, clearly labeled, that can now appear in response to a follow-up question inside a back-and-forth AI Mode conversation, not just the first query. Google says it will expand ads in AI Mode to Brazil, Mexico and the UK in Q4 2026.

Why it mattersthis moves the ad further into the conversation itself, the same territory ChatGPT has been testing with its own conversational ads (issues 16-19). Whoever controls the follow-up question controls a second, third and fourth chance to show an ad inside what the user still experiences as a single, continuous answer.
UNA Media Hub, Intersections 2026 Milan / spotandweb.it · October 28, 2026

Italy's ad market grows 2.7%, but 88.6% of pure digital spend goes straight to platforms

UNA (Aziende della Comunicazione Unite) presented new estimates putting Italy's 2026 advertising market at 12.6 billion euros, up 2.7%, outpacing the 0.9% GDP growth forecast for the country. Video leads with 6.65 billion euros (52.7% of the market, +6.5%); text-based advertising is 5.44 billion (43.1%, +2.3%); audio is flat at 527 million (4.2%, -0.1%). Within "pure digital" (6.4 billion euros, after stripping out Advanced TV, Digital Out-of-Home, Digital Print and Digital Audio from the wider 7.8 billion "expanded digital" figure), UNA estimates 88.6% of spend, roughly 5.7 billion euros, goes to platforms rather than Italian publishers. Retail Media in Italy is now worth 640 million euros, per separate UPA data cited in the same report.

Why it mattersthis is the Italian, numbered version of the same story running through issue 20's Omnicom and Braze deals: growth in a market doesn't mean growth for the people making the content. Italian publishers are producing journalism into a digital ad market where fewer than 12 cents of every "pure digital" euro stays with them.
ppc.land · reporting through October 8, 2026

Apple still hasn't given a public release date for the Safari fix that would unblock The Trade Desk

Apple asked The Trade Desk to test an iOS 27.2 beta build on October 5 that appears to remove the adsrvr.org domain from Safari's ad-tech blocklist, the block that's cut off Trade Desk's ability to serve ads to Safari users since iOS 27 shipped September 14 (issues 15-19). But as of ppc.land's October 8 reporting, the underlying bug tracker still showed status "NEW," neither company had confirmed on the record that the domain was actually removed, and Apple had given no date for when iOS 27.2 itself would ship to ordinary users. A beta fix is not a shipped fix.

Why it matterssix weeks after the block first went live, the people closest to the problem still can't say with certainty whether it's fixed or when regular iPhone users will see the change, a reminder that platform rules enforced through an opaque blocklist can be just as opaque to roll back.

Campaigns & brand moves

cosmeticsbusiness.com / thezoereport.com · October 27, 2026

Jennifer Lawrence launches mes°, a haircare brand she co-designed with a biotech company

mes° launched October 27 as a partnership between Lawrence and Jasmina Aganovic, founder of biotech beauty company Arcaea (backed with $78 million in Series A funding from Chanel, Givaudan and Olaplex among others). The brand's "unbothered beauty" positioning centers on three biodesigned, multifunctional products, priced $34-52, meant to extend a hairstyle beyond a single wash, sold exclusively at mesbeauty.com.

Why it mattersLawrence isn't fronting a formula someone else built, she's attached to the actual R&D company behind it, the same move several top creators have been making since issue 12's thread on trading one-off brand deals for equity and real operating roles. The credibility being sold here is scientific, not just famous.
hypebae.com · collection live October 27, 2026

True Religion and Baby Phat revive Y2K with two Love Island faces

True Religion and Baby Phat released their first joint capsule, fronted by Love Island USA's Aniya Harvey and Kayda Bosse, built around low-rise flared and bootcut denim, shrunken satin bombers, faux-fur-trimmed halters and rhinestones, fusing True Religion's 2000s denim codes with Kimora Lee Simmons' original Baby Phat glam. The capsule went on sale October 27 at both brands' sites, after being unveiled October 20.

Why it matterstwo different kinds of nostalgia, Y2K hip-hop glamour and this year's reality-TV stars, are stacked on the same product instead of picking one or the other, a bet that two separate fan bases will both recognize themselves in it.
spotandweb.it · debuted October 29, 2026 at Lucca Comics & Games

Findus turns its decades-old mascot into an official comic book

"Capitan Findus - Il tesoro dell'aquila," the first official comic starring Findus's longtime advertising mascot, debuted at Lucca Comics & Games 2026, made with the Scuola Internazionale di Comics. The project grew out of a 2024 creative contest where Findus had thirty young illustrators reinterpret Capitan Findus, put five finalists' work on limited-edition Bastoncini packaging, and let consumers vote; winner Matteo Montanari drew the finished comic, with a special cover by Giuseppe Camuncoli. A thousand limited copies were distributed at Lucca Comics; wider distribution follows in 2027 through Panini.

Why it mattersthis is McDonald's "own your IP instead of renting someone else's platform" logic (issue 20) running in reverse and in miniature: Findus already owns a 1970s advertising character people recognize, and instead of letting him stay a static logo, it's investing to turn him into an actual ongoing story, with Panini's distribution network doing in 2027 what FIFA's platform used to do for McDonald's.

What is working in content

Radar SWG, week of Oct 19-25 / spotandweb.it · October 27, 2026

Italians are pulling back from loud branding, and the data has real numbers behind it

SWG found that 38% of Italians have stopped following, ignored or avoided a brand in the past twelve months because they found its advertising excessive. On logo visibility, 25% prefer a discreet logo and another 25% prefer none at all, against just 6% who want a highly visible one (44% say it doesn't affect their choice; Gen Z breaks the other way, with 40% preferring a recognizable logo). 55% consider it inappropriate to flaunt branded products openly during a period of economic difficulty (66% among Baby Boomers, 33% among Gen Z), and 66% overall want well-known brands to show more awareness of the economic and social context when they advertise. Asked what they actually want from brands: 37% say durable, reliable quality first, 26% fair labor conditions, 21% affordability, 17% transparent communication, and 14% simply less advertising pressure.

Why it mattersthis is a direct, numbered answer to the same question the Reddit/Pinterest/WPP split above is asking from the platform side: audiences are rewarding restraint and punishing volume. A brand chasing maximum exposure in Italy right now is working against what more than a third of the audience already says it wants.
vaizle.com, single-source aggregator data, flagged as such · observed October 2026

The multi-character debate format is turning product skepticism into content instead of hiding from it

Creators film three distinct personas, typically a skeptic, an enthusiast and a pragmatist, in the same outfit with only expression and posture changed between takes, then cut between them every 3-5 seconds; Reels using this rhythm are reported 72% more likely to go viral, and versions under 30 seconds get the highest completion rates. Beauty brand Minimalist is cited using it directly on price objections: one character questions the cost, another explains the ingredient sourcing, the third shows the result.

Why it mattersinstead of scripting away a customer's doubt, the format stages the doubt on screen and answers it in character, which reads as more honest than a straight sell precisely because it admits the objection exists.

Social trends

tokchart.com · tracked through October 28, 2026

"MAFIA" by Soothewave becomes TikTok's #1 global sound seven months after it first appeared

The track first showed up on TikTok April 18, 2026, and spent months building before becoming the single most-used sound on the platform worldwide as of October 28, with more than 1.54 million videos and still adding close to 18,000 new videos in a single day. It's strongest in the US, Indonesia and Malaysia. Maturity: hot, a slow seven-month build that just hit its peak rather than a sound that spiked and will fade fast.

Why it mattersmost trend coverage chases what's brand new; this is a reminder that TikTok's own internal momentum can take months to compound before a sound actually becomes the platform's biggest, which argues for watching slow climbers, not just this week's spike.
tokchart.com · tracked through October 2026

"Dame Hombro" turns a street freestyle filmed outside a restaurant in Spain into a global AI dance trend

The song, released October 7 by Dominican dembow artist Bulin 47 with Kevin Wai and Breyco En Producidera, comes from a real, unplanned street freestyle video; the sound has been used in more than 193,300 TikTok videos since October 8, and is the #1 song in both Ecuador and Puerto Rico. An AI photo-to-video effect lets anyone turn a still photo into a dancer doing Bulin 47 and Kevin Wai's signature shoulder-bounce choreography, with Venezuela alone accounting for a third of videos. Maturity: nascent, three weeks old and still climbing.

Why it mattersthe trend didn't start as a marketing asset, it started as two people genuinely freestyling on a sidewalk, and TikTok's own AI tooling is what turned that unplanned moment into a repeatable, global format within weeks.

The historical bridge

Lynn, Massachusetts, 1870s-1880s

A widow sold more medicine with other women's letters than with any slogan

Lydia E. Pinkham's Vegetable Compound, first sold in 1875, became one of the best-selling patent medicines of the 19th century largely because of what the company did with its mail. Unsolicited testimonial letters from women poured in, reportedly up to 150 a day at the business's peak, describing relief from menstrual and menopausal symptoms; Pinkham personally read and answered many of them in strict confidence through a dedicated "Department of Advice," promising women no man would ever read what they wrote. Her own portrait went on the product label and on give-away trade cards printed "Put this in your album," making her, by most accounts, the first woman whose face was used this way in American advertising. Some of the letters were published as testimonials in company pamphlets. The company kept answering letters "from Mrs. Pinkham" for years after her death in 1883, a practice that drew public skepticism once a 1905 Ladies' Home Journal article showed readers her gravestone.

Why it still holds. Pinkham's compound didn't out-advertise its competitors with a bigger slogan, it out-trusted them by building something that looked and felt like a community of women talking to each other, with the company itself positioned as a trusted confidante rather than a billboard. A hundred and fifty years later, Reddit turned the same basic mechanic, people trusting other people's voices over a brand's, into $895 million of quarterly revenue, while a platform built on exposure instead of trust (WPP's roster of agencies, still selling reach) posted growth of half a percent.
